# California Security Deposit Dispute Checklist

## What to do first after a San Diego move-out
Your strongest position is that California generally requires landlords to return the deposit balance and provide an itemized statement within **21 days** of move-out, and charges must be tied to actual cleaning/repair beyond ordinary wear and tear.

- Keep your move-out date, lease, deposit amount, and landlord’s deduction notice together in one folder.
- Save the photos from move-out day, the lease, any inspection notes, and all texts/emails.
- Compare the landlord’s claims against California’s rules on cleaning, painting, and normal wear.
- Ask for proof: invoices, receipts, and a clear explanation of why each charge was needed.
- If the deduction looks unsupported, request the full **$600** back in writing and set a short deadline.
- If the landlord does not resolve it, consider small claims court and bring your photos and documents.

## Dispute Plan and Email Draft
| Step | Action | What to check | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm the timeline | Move-out date was 2026-03-31; deposit statement should arrive within 21 days | You can show any delay or missing statement |
| 2 | Review the deduction reasons | Cleaning and repainting must be more than ordinary wear and tear | Weak or vague charges become challenge points |
| 3 | Match photos to claims | Compare broom-clean photos to each alleged issue | Photos support that the unit was left reasonably clean |
| 4 | Ask for documentation | Request itemized costs, receipts, invoices, and scope of work | Landlord must justify the $600 deduction |
| 5 | Demand the balance | Request refund of any unsupported amount, including the full $600 if no proof exists | You create a clear written record |
| 6 | Escalate if needed | Send a final demand, then small claims if unresolved | You preserve your right to recover the money |

**Draft email**

Subject: Request for Itemized Security Deposit Statement and Refund

Dear [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I am writing regarding my security deposit for the apartment at [address]. I moved out on 2026-03-31 at the end of my 12-month lease, and I understand that $600 was withheld from my $1,800 deposit for cleaning and repainting.

I dispute this deduction. I left the unit in broom-clean condition, and I have move-out photos documenting the condition of the apartment on the day I vacated. Based on my understanding of California law, deductions must reflect actual, necessary costs beyond ordinary wear and tear and should be supported by an itemized explanation.

Please send me:
- A detailed itemized statement showing each charge
- Copies of all invoices, receipts, and supporting documents
- An explanation of why the cleaning and repainting were necessary
- Refund of any amount not properly supported, including the disputed $600 if no valid documentation exists

Please respond in writing within 10 calendar days of this email. If we cannot resolve this promptly, I will consider all available remedies to recover the withheld funds.

Thank you,
[Your full name]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Forwarding address]
